intro.title: Separating Thoughts from Facts
description: The fierce waves crashing over you right now were stirred up by a wind called 'thoughts.'
To keep from being swept away, you need to step back from the wind shaking your surface.
Simply realizing that the wind is what creates the waves—that alone begins to weaken the grip of anxiety.
intro.contentDescription: A practice of understanding that thoughts and facts are separate, and learning to tell them apart.
steps: 1. Write it down: Write the thoughts that make you anxious as a sentence.
2. Separate the thoughts: Drag and select the parts that are 'your thoughts,' not facts.
3. Let them go: Watch the selected thoughts fade away, leaving only the objective facts behind.
intro.tip: Tip: The wind can shake your surface, but it can never reach the depths of your ocean. Just quietly watch the wind as it blows by.

title: What thoughts are
floating in your mind?
step1.description: Without judging, write down the voices in your head exactly as they sound. Long or short, any sentence is fine.
step1.placeholder: e.g., "I'll never get anything right," "What if everyone hates me?"

title: How much of this sentence
is just a 'thought'?
step2.description: Drag and select only the interpretation or judgment.

result.title: You've separated the waves from the wind
description: Just like the text that turned transparent, the wind of thoughts only brushes past your ocean for a moment.
As the wind loses its strength, the rough waves will soon settle into calm.
